questions.q: Why are a Deployment's Pods described as deliberately interchangeable?
options: Because Deployments do not support rolling updates
They get randomly generated name suffixes with no guaranteed identity, and any replica can be removed when scaling down
Because every Pod in a Deployment must run on the same node
Because Deployments cannot use PersistentVolumeClaims at all
questions.explain: Deployment Pods have no stable identity — names are randomly suffixed, and scaling down can remove any replica, which is fine for stateless workloads but wrong for a clustered database where each replica plays a distinct role.

questions.q: What two guarantees does a StatefulSet provide that a Deployment does not?
options: Automatic horizontal autoscaling and automatic image updates
Stable, predictable Pod names/network identity, and a dedicated PersistentVolumeClaim per replica
Built-in database replication logic and automatic backups
Guaranteed placement on a specific node and GPU scheduling
questions.explain: A StatefulSet gives Pods stable names like postgres-0, postgres-1 that persist across restarts, plus a PVC created per-replica from volumeClaimTemplates — both of which a Deployment's interchangeable Pods lack.

questions.q: What does `volumeClaimTemplates` actually do in a StatefulSet spec?
options: It deletes all PVCs automatically when the StatefulSet is deleted
It creates one shared PVC that every replica Pod mounts simultaneously
It defines a Secret used to authenticate to the storage backend
It stamps out one separate PVC per replica, named by convention like pgdata-postgres-0, pgdata-postgres-1
questions.explain: volumeClaimTemplates generates a dedicated PVC per replica instead of sharing one — this is what solves the ReadWriteOnce multi-replica mounting problem from the PV/PVC lesson.

questions.q: The Pod `postgres-1` is deleted (e.g. due to a node failure) and recreated by the StatefulSet. What happens to its storage?
options: The new postgres-1 Pod binds back to the same pgdata-postgres-1 PVC and the same underlying data
A brand-new empty PVC is created for the new postgres-1 Pod
The new postgres-1 Pod binds to whichever PVC happens to be unbound at the time
All PVCs in the StatefulSet are reshuffled across the remaining replicas
questions.explain: Each replica's PVC is tied to its stable name. The new postgres-1 Pod reattaches to pgdata-postgres-1 and its existing data, which a Deployment's interchangeable Pods could never guarantee.

questions.q: Why must a StatefulSet's `serviceName` point at a headless Service (`clusterIP: None`)?
options: Headless Services are required for any StorageClass to work
A headless Service is the only type that supports ReadWriteOnce volumes
It gives each Pod its own resolvable DNS name instead of load-balancing traffic across all replicas, which matters when clients need to reach a specific replica
It disables ordered startup so all replicas can start simultaneously
questions.explain: A headless Service skips load-balancing and instead lets DNS resolve each Pod individually, e.g. postgres-0.postgres.default.svc.cluster.local — essential when a client needs to target a specific replica, such as the primary for writes.
